podcast.body: Ralph Hütter and Florian Schneider traveled to the United States to handle the production and mastering of this album independently. Upon their return, Karl Bartos discovered the final version of the record only after it had already been manufactured, highlighting the independent and exclusive control maintained by the two founders over significant aspects of the band's output. "cuando salía el Transiro de Plexpress, que Ralph Yfloria se van a Estados Unidos a realizar la producción y masterización vuelven, y el propio Calvarto Siel descubre en la versión final del disco cuando ya está fabricada."

Released in 1977, this album by Kraftwerk is described as massively influential. Over more than 30 years since its release, it has impacted a wide range of genres, including dance music, industrial noise, rap, and hip hop. Its sounds were considered "weird" and "alien," inspiring numerous other artists. "In the 30 plus years since it came out, this record has influenced everything from dance music to industrial noise to rap and hip hop."

podcast.body: Released in 1977, this album is noted for its influential beats, which were foundational in creating hip hop music. Its distinctive rhythms were famously sampled and adapted by artists like Afrika Bambaataa for "Planet Rock." "Craftwork beats, especially from their 1977 album Trans-Europe Express, were influential in creating the foundations of hip hop."

podcast.body: The lyrics of this album contain a subtle nod to David Bowie and Iggy Pop, referencing their residency in Berlin and the idea of visiting them. This lyric serves as a small, curious confirmation of the cultural presence of Bowie and Pop in Berlin during this period. "en el tranchiro Pespés de Crabbro en 1977, en la letra se hace referencia a que David Bowie y Hip-Hop estaban viviendo en Berlin y los iban a visitar."

podcast.body: This album was specifically envisioned by Kraftwerk, leading them to commission the development of the Syntanorma sequencer to achieve its distinctive sound and marking a significant stylistic shift for the band. "fue inventado específicamente para que Grabbar quisiés el trans-Europe express."

podcast.body: This album, along with "The Man-Machine," solidified Kraftwerk's electronic pop language and became a worldwide success. Its evocative melodies were famously sampled by Afrika Bambaataa for "Planet Rock," a foundational track in electro and hip-hop. The album dealt with terrestrial communications, anticipating digital communications explored in "Computer World." "Translíope Express, lanzado en 1977 y demand machine de 1978, acabado de dar la forma definitiva a esa idea y fueron un éxito en medio mundo."
